experience.summary: An AI research assistant on energy access in Africa that cites a curated library of sector reports. Team of 4. Sole engineer for the first month, now owning the backend, AI pipeline and infrastructure.
highlights: Built retrieval in PostgreSQL without a separate vector database: pgvector semantic search (HNSW) and keyword search, merged with reciprocal rank fusion. Keyword search catches specialist terms that semantic matching misses.
Built the answering service in Python (FastAPI) without LangChain or similar. It calls Claude through AWS Bedrock, streams inline citations, and declines questions the library cannot support.
Built document ingestion on Redis Streams with consumer groups, parallel workers and a dead-letter stream, so large PDFs are embedded without slowing the API.
Isolated each organisation's data with PostgreSQL row-level security, and tracked token usage per organisation.

Wrote the CloudFormation stacks for three containerised services (chat API, query service, ingestion service) on ECS Fargate, reducing environment setup from days to under fifteen minutes. Three junior engineers set the project up alone after one onboarding call.

Built a pull request review agent used by the Access to Energy and Hoppers teams. It combines two models' reviews, posts first-pass feedback, and flags me only when they disagree. A human still approves every merge.

experience.position: Full Stack Software Engineer (Contract, Part Time)
experience.summary: Event ticketing platform. Built the payment handling and the ticket reservation flow.
highlights: Built payment handling for two providers (DPO, IoTec) with idempotent webhooks that use row-level locking to stop duplicate charges. Recorded settlements and booking fee snapshots for reconciliation.

Stopped double booking by claiming a ticket with `select_for_update` in a short transaction, then holding it with a reserved status and expiry until payment succeeds or the hold lapses. Purchase limits are enforced in the same flow.
Delivered features across the Django backend, React admin panel and Flutter app, including QR ticketing with server-side validation and team permissions. Errors are tracked in Sentry.

experience.summary: Promoted to Senior in March 2023. Stepped away in May 2025 to complete MSc in Data Analytics full time.
highlights: Owned three client-facing products end to end: the candidate assessment platform (the games candidates take), the recruiter portal and client analytics dashboards, built in Django, PostgreSQL and React.
Led delivery for a team of five for about two months after our manager was let go with no handover, alongside a full workload. The team met every sprint commitment and shipped on time.
Pushed back on deprecating a database table in one sprint. I specced where it was still used (production writing, the warehouse reading) and proposed a staged plan, preventing a production break.
Built candidate scoring on Celery queues with RabbitMQ, and a fan-out exchange to two services with idempotent consumers.
Took over the Snowflake and dbt pipeline behind the dashboards when the data scientist left, and agreed what counts as a completed assessment (12 of 16 games) with product and data science.

Treated a broken assessment game as severity one because it stalled a candidate's job application: fixed and shipped straight away, monitored with New Relic. Took turns on a two week investigation rotation, including data migrations made safe with backups, undo scripts and staging runs.
Ran 15+ technical interviews against an existing rubric, and wrote onboarding documentation for systems where I had become the bottleneck.
Built the assessment games candidates take, used by around 500,000 candidates a day, including accessibility accommodations (colour blindness, dyslexia font, extra time).

Fixed an N+1 query problem for a client with 120,000+ records. The endpoint went from 8 to 12 seconds to under 800ms and queries per page from 100+ to 3 to 5, with the record count cached for 30 minutes.
Automated the micro-frontend deploy on push (GitHub Actions, S3, CloudFront). Manual work fell from about twenty minutes to under five, and deployment errors from about five a quarter to none.
Moved New Relic logs from plain strings to searchable key-value fields.
